# dsh-code-git-workbench

A Code and Git workbench for the **DeepSeek Harness Web UI**. It adds two pages
to the right Sidebar

Code and Git workbench for the **DeepSeek Harness Web UI**. It adds two pages
to the right Sidebar:

- **Code** — a lazy file tree for a Harness workspace, file tabs, a CodeMirror
editor, syntax highli

ghting, search, reload and save.
- **Git** — a PyCharm-style log: local/remote branches, a commit gr

aph, commit
details, file diffs, checkout, merge, rebase, cherry-pick, reset, revert, tags
and fetch

details, file diffs, checkout, merge, rebase, cherry-pick, reset, revert, tags
and fetch/pull/push.

It also keeps running subagents above idle ones in the header's subagent catalog
popup.

The plugin is host + client code for DeepSeek Harness. It has no build step and
no dependency on VS

Code. The PyCharm-style Git UI is shared in source form with
the companion VS Code extension
pycharm

-git-log; the two
repositories remain independent at runtime.
## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness with the bundled plugin CLI (tested on the 0.2.1-rc.2 /
DSH 44.x desktop build).

- A local Git repository for the Git page.
- Node.js is **not** required to install or run the plugi

A local Git repository for the Git page.

## Use

1. Open a session. The pages start from the session's workspace; Code can switch
to any Harness work

space, Git to any workspace that is a Git repository.
2. Open the right Sidebar (`Ctrl+Alt+B` on the

desktop build, or the sidebar
button).
3. Click `+` → **Code** or **Git**. The guide also lists bot

h pages.
4. For more room, use the panel's fullscreen control.
### Code

- Lazy directory tree; `.git` is hidden.
- The workspace selector in the tree header lists every Har

ness workspace. When
the session directory is not a repository, Code starts in the first workspace
t

hat is one. The choice is remembered per session.
- Tabs keep their own document, cursor, scroll pos

ition and dirty state.
- **Autosave** is on, modelled after PyCharm:
- idle for 2 seconds after the

last edit — every dirty tab is written;
- switching to another application / hiding the DSH window;

- closing a file tab (the tab is saved, not discarded);
- switching the workspace (all dirty tabs ar

example Git) blurs the editor and triggers a
save, which covers the “before VCS operation” case.
Sw

itching between file tabs does **not** force a save; the idle/focus/close
triggers do, just like PyC

harm. `Ctrl+S` still saves manually; the status bar
shows `Auto-saved` after a successful write.
- `

Ctrl+R` reloads the active file. The toolbar has Save and Reload actions.
- CodeMirror offers line n

umbers, bracket matching, auto-close, incremental
search (`Ctrl+F`) and modes for JS/TS, Python, JSO

N, Markdown, HTML/CSS, YAML,
SQL, shell, PowerShell and C-like languages.
- Files are read and writt

en as UTF-8. Files larger than 2 MB and binary files
are rejected for display.
### Git

- Repository selector for every workspace that is a Git repository.
- Branch tree with local/remote

groups, filter, current branch, ahead/behind,
checkout, checkout + rebase, merge, rebase, compare, p

ush, rename, delete and
tag actions.
- Slash-separated branch names become expandable folders: `feat

/123-login` is
shown as `feat` → `123-login`. The tree is built independently inside Local
and Remot

e. With a single remote, its name is treated as context and stripped
from the folder path; with seve

ral remotes, the remote name becomes the first
folder. Folder expansion is remembered per repository

.
- Branches can be starred from the row or from the context menu. Favorites float

## Architecture
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The host API applies `ctx.connection.requestRejection(req)` to every request, so
it inherits the Har

ness Host/Origin fence and browser authentication. All routes
are same-origin:
a browser talks to the same listener directly.
API surface:
| Route | Purpose |

| `GET /code-git/api/context` | session cwd, selected root, workspaces, repo status |
| `GET /code-g

it/api/tree` | one directory level |
| `GET/PUT /code-git/api/file` | read/write one file |
| `GET /

code-git/api/git/state` | branches, commits, refs, ahead/behind |
| `GET /code-git/api/git/status` |

staged, unstaged and untracked files |
| `GET /code-git/api/git/worktree-diff` | index/HEAD/working

tree file contents |
| `GET /code-git/api/git/commit` | commit message, parents, file stats |
| `GE

T /code-git/api/git/diff` | old/new file contents |
| `POST /code-git/api/git/action` | checkout, me
rge, rebase, reset, fetch, pull branch, push, … |

Every request is checked against the session's registered workspaces; paths are
resolved and confine

d to the selected root. Git runs through `execFile` without
a shell, with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`.

The Git UI is the same HTML/CSS/JS as the companion VS Code extension's panel.
`web/git/bridge.js` i

mplements the small `acquireVsCodeApi()` surface the UI was
written against and maps its messages to

the JSON API. No VS Code runtime is
involved.
